title: How would you estimate how many dentists the UK needs?
description: A step-by-step estimate for "How many dentists does the UK need?" with the approach, the maths and a sanity check.
hook: A capacity question: how many check-ups the country needs, divided by how many one dentist can do. Have a go at your own estimate before reading on.
body:
The question

How many dentists does the UK need?

The approach

Check-ups needed per year ÷ check-ups one dentist can do per year.

Tip: When you finish, say what the number means for the client, not just the number.

Step by step

  1. People in the UK: 68M
  2. × 70% go to the dentist
  3. × 2 visits each per year
  4. ÷ 2,640 visits one dentist handles per year (12 a day, 220 days)

That gives about 36.1k dentists.

Does it make sense?

About one dentist per 1,900 people. Treatments beyond check-ups would push the number needed up.

Real-world check

The UK population was about 69.3 million at mid-2024 (ONS). This example rounds to 68 million, which is fine: in an interview, any sensible round number is accepted as long as you say it.

Source: ONS: UK population estimates, mid-2024.

A capacity model needs treatments, not just check-ups

The shortcut gives approximately 36,000 full-time-equivalent dentists for routine appointments. It does not yet cover longer fillings, emergency work, root canals, surgical procedures or the administrative time between patients. For example, if routine appointments use 60% of dentist clinical time, you cannot assign the remaining 40% to more check-ups while also expecting the dentist to perform treatments.

A better version uses clinical hours. Estimate annual hours per patient for preventative, restorative and specialist care, then divide by productive clinical hours per dentist. Separate dentists from hygienists and therapists if the question is about the total dental workforce.

Public and private service availability, geographical distribution and waiting times complicate any national average. A country can have enough clinicians in aggregate yet have a severe shortage in particular towns. State what "need" means: demand for appointments, funded posts or the workforce required to meet a service standard.
